name_note: GTDB's Eubacterium_G is a split of the classical genus Eubacterium; the catalog genomes it holds carry NCBI names Eubacterium, and Eubacterium ventriosum is the named species in it, so the literature below is about that species rather than the whole classical genus.

sentences.text: Eubacterium ventriosum is an anaerobic commensal bacterium of the Firmicutes, detected in human faecal samples by shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
A study of 159 Chongqing residents split into young, middle-aged and elderly groups reported the Eubacterium ventriosum group enriched in the young adults.

A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study reported that higher genetically predicted abundance of the genus Eubacterium ventriosum group was associated with lower risk of irritable bowel syndrome.
In treated chronic hepatitis B, Eubacterium ventriosum was among anaerobic commensals showing nominal group-related differences that did not remain significant after FDR correction.
